bugLogs.title: Insufficient color contrast on Checkout button text
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Open the product listing page in a web browser.
3. Use a contrast‑checking tool (e.g., WebAIM Contrast Checker) to inspect the button's text color (#ffffff) against its background color (#28a745).
4. Observe that the reported contrast ratio is 3.13:1, which is below the required 4.5:1 for normal text.
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The button text must have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background, per WCAG 2.1 Success Criterion 1.4.3.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The button text has a contrast ratio of 3.13:1 (foreground #ffffff, background #28a745), failing the minimum contrast requirement.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Adjust the color values to meet the 4.5:1 ratio. For example, change the button background to a darker shade such as #1e7e34, or change the text color to a darker gray like #212529. Verify the new colors achieve at least 4.5:1 contrast using a contrast checker.

bugLogs.title: Missing lang attribute on <html> element
affected_users: users who rely on language detection
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Open the affected e‑commerce page in a browser.
2. Open the developer tools and inspect the <html> element.
3. Observe that the <html> tag does not contain a lang attribute.
bugLogs.expected_behavior: The <html> element must include a lang attribute that correctly identifies the primary language of the page (e.g., <html lang="en">).
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The <html> element is rendered without any lang attribute.
bugLogs.suggested_fix:
Add a lang attribute to the <html> tag with the appropriate language code, e.g.,
html
<html lang="en">

If the site supports multiple languages, ensure the attribute reflects the current language context and consider adding xml:lang for XHTML compatibility.

bugLogs.title: Thumbnail images missing alternative text
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Navigate to the product listing page where the shoe thumbnails are displayed.
2. Observe the two thumbnail images: shoe-red-thumb.jpg and shoe-blue-thumb.jpg.
3. Use a screen reader (e.g., NVDA, VoiceOver) to navigate the page.
4. Notice that the screen reader announces "image" with no description for each thumbnail.
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Each element must have a text alternative that conveys its purpose (e.g., alt="Red shoe thumbnail") or be marked as decorative with alt="" and role="presentation".
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The elements are coded as and with no alt, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or role attributes.
bugLogs.suggested_fix: Add descriptive alt attributes to the images, for example: html If the images are purely decorative, use an empty alt and role="presentation": html

bugLogs.title: Numeric inputs lack associated labels
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Open the product page containing the quantity selector.
2. Locate the numeric input element with value="1" (e.g., <input type="number" value="1" ...>).
3. Observe that no <label>, aria-label, aria-labelledby, title, or placeholder is associated with the input.
4. Repeat steps 2‑3 for the numeric input with value="2".
bugLogs.expected_behavior: Each form control must have a programmatically determinable name via a visible <label> element (or an explicit aria-label/aria-labelledby) so that assistive technologies can announce the purpose of the input.
bugLogs.actual_behavior: The <input type="number" value="1"> and <input type="number" value="2"> elements have no associated <label>, no aria-label, no aria-labelledby, no title, and no placeholder, violating WCAG 3.3.2.
bugLogs.suggested_fix:
Add a visible label for each input and associate it using the for/id pattern, e.g.,
html
<label for="qty-1">Quantity</label>
<input id="qty-1" type="number" value="1" min="1" max="10" style="width:50px;" aria-required="true">

If a visible label cannot be used, provide an accessible name with aria-label or aria-labelledby. Ensure the label text clearly describes the purpose (e.g., "Quantity").
